subject: Marketplace private offer pricing — unit price mapping & token volume follow-up
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
To: Daniel Kim <daniel@brightcart.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 15 Mar 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Marketplace private offer pricing — unit price mapping & token volume follow-up

Hi Daniel —

Thanks again for the call earlier — really appreciate you walking through BrightCart’s marketplace plans. Quick recap and the asks we discussed so we can get you a clean private-offer price mapping for AWS/GCP/Azure: 

Key points from the call:
- You’re planning to list Redwood as a private offer on AWS Marketplace first, followed by GCP and Azure later in the quarter.
- Expected initial GA usage: ~500M tokens/month, ramp to ~3B tokens/month within 6–9 months (mix of chat + generation).
- Goal budget range for the first 6 months: $50k–$150k (total spend across cloud marketplace private offers).
- Target unit economics: you mentioned a target of ~$22–$35 per 1M tokens on marketplace private offers once platform fees are included.

Action items we discussed I’ll own:
1) Provide a unit price mapping for AWS/GCP/Azure private offer flows (what the end-customer sees vs our list/discount and typical marketplace fees).
2) Suggest a recommended unit price / $ per 1M tokens target for BrightCart at each volume tier (starter, scale, enterprise).
3) Share a model workbook with the Gross-to-Net mapping and an example DocuSign flow for Marketplace private offers.

Could you confirm the volume mix (approx % chat vs. single-shot generation) and whether you expect embeddings or reranking traffic in the first 3 months? That helps us recommend the right price tiers and any quantization/throughput recommendations.

I’m attaching a baseline mapping workbook we use internally — I’ll populate it with BrightCart numbers once I get the usage split and confirmation on whether BrightCart prefers a per-token or per-request unit for some of the high-rate endpoints.

Next steps: if you can send the usage report/forecast (CSV or the Q1 PDF you mentioned) I’ll run the numbers and get back with a price map and recommended target $/1M tokens by Friday. Looping in Aditya (SE) to review latency/throughput constraints for marketplace SKUs.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Enterprise Sales | Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.ai | +1 (555) 212-9987

Attachments: redwood_unit_price_mapping.xlsx (workbook)

From: Daniel Kim <daniel@brightcart.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
Cc: AWS Marketplace Ops <aws-marketplace-ops@amazon.com>
Date: Mon, 15 Mar 2027 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Marketplace private offer pricing — unit price mapping & token volume follow-up

Marissa —

Thanks for the summary and the sheet — very helpful. Quick answers below: 

- Volume mix: right now we project ~70% chat (avg 150 tokens per convo) and ~30% single-shot generation (avg 450 tokens), embeddings negligible in the first 90 days (~1–2% of traffic).
- Q1 usage report attached (exported from our telemetry) — see brightcart_usage_report_q1.pdf for the month-by-month baseline and a 6-month internal forecast.
- We definitely prefer a per-token unit pricing on the marketplace side (cleaner for our procurement team).
- The $22–$35 /1M tokens target you referenced sounds roughly in line with what procurement expects on marketplace private offers after gross-to-net adjustments, though we have flexibility for volume tiers.

We’re happy to proceed with the AWS private offer first. Can you lay out: (a) list price to publish on AWS, (b) private-offer net price (what we and our customers pay), and (c) how that maps back to Redwood’s revenue after AWS fees? If you can show that per 1M token bucket (0–1M, 1–10M, 10–100M, 100M+), that’d be ideal.

Happy to hop back on a quick 20-min call if that helps.

Cheers,
Daniel Kim
Head of Partnerships | BrightCart
D: +1 (415) 555-0190
daniel@brightcart.com

Attachment: brightcart_usage_report_q1.pdf

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
To: Daniel Kim <daniel@brightcart.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 16 Mar 2027 10:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Marketplace private offer pricing — unit price mapping & token volume follow-up

Thanks Daniel — got the usage report and that’s perfect. I’ve started populating the workbook with BrightCart’s forecast and prepared an initial gross-to-net mapping for AWS private offers. High-level preliminary recommendations below (we’ll include a detailed per-bucket sheet in the workbook):

Preliminary unit price guidance (net to BrightCart / customer-facing):
- Starter (0–1M tokens): list price $40 / 1M, private-offer net $36 / 1M (Redwood list $30 / 1M + marketplace uplift/fees)
- Scale (1–10M tokens): list price $30 / 1M, private-offer net $27 / 1M (Redwood list $22 / 1M + marketplace fees)
- Growth (10–100M tokens): list price $25 / 1M, private-offer net $22.5 / 1M (Redwood list $18 / 1M + marketplace fees)
- Enterprise (100M+ tokens): list price $18 / 1M, private-offer net $16.2 / 1M (Redwood list $13 / 1M + marketplace fees/commissions)

Notes/assumptions:
- Marketplace fees vary by cloud and region; AWS typically charges a referral/transaction fee that effectively increases the list price required to achieve a target net. The mapping above assumes AWS referral of ~12–15% for private offers; we’ll run GCP/Azure comparables in the workbook.
- These net numbers are what we expect BrightCart to see as the per-1M price on your invoice when the private offer is accepted. Redwood’s revenue (gross after we pay marketplace fees) is the ‘Redwood list’ line.
- At your forecasted ramp (500M -> 3B tokens), the $/1M realized should push into the Growth/Enterprise tiers — that’s where you get the biggest unit economics benefit.

Next steps I’ll take before Friday:
- Finalize the workbook with per-cloud fee assumptions (AWS/GCP/Azure) and a side-by-side unit-price mapping.
- Add a sensitivity tab that shows realized Redwood revenue at the volumes you provided (and the impact of a 10% vs 15% marketplace fee).
- Prepare a suggested DocuSign flow + line-items for the private offer template.

Aditya — can you validate the latency/throughput assumptions for the 3B token/month target and confirm any recommended instance sizing for the marketplace SKUs? If we need to recommend reserved/dedicated capacity vs hosted API for best latency at scale, flag that so we can include a cost delta in the workbook.

Daniel — if you want this in a quick call, I can do 20 mins tomorrow morning PT.

Best,
Marissa

Attachments: redwood_unit_price_mapping.xlsx (populated draft)

From: Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.ai>
To: Daniel Kim <daniel@brightcart.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 17 Mar 2027 14:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Marketplace private offer pricing — unit price mapping & token volume follow-up

Hey team —

I reviewed the forecast and Marissa’s mapping. Quick technical qual notes: 
- 3B tokens/month (steady-state) with ~70/30 chat/gen mix: recommend a Dedicated pool (reserved capacity) for consistent latency and predictable throughput; hosted API could work during initial months but will be more unpredictable at scale.
- For marketplace SKUs we typically publish the same model family but call out recommended capacity tiers in the offer docs (e.g., "Recommended: Redwood Dedicated - S1 for up to 1B tokens/month; D2 for 1B–5B").
- Latency/instance guidance: for chat-heavy workloads targeting p95 < 400ms we recommend a mix of tensor-optimized instances and our batching config; I’ll add concrete instance types and expected cost deltas to the workbook.

I attached a short SE note and the instance-sizing tab to the workbook (see redwood_unit_price_mapping.xlsx). Happy to jump on a call to walk through the workbook.

Thanks,
Aditya Rao
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
aditya@redwood.ai
